description: One pest management consultant, and which commodity they advise on. A CHILD TABLE RATHER THAN A LINK BECAUSE ONE IS THE EXCEPTION HERE, NOT THE RULE: a farm running pome fruit and cherries commonly has a different consultant for each, and a single Link on the Company would hold whichever was typed last. Left with no commodity, a row means the consultant covers the whole operation.

fields.description: The consulting firm or licensed consultant, as a Supplier — because that is who they already are on these books, and a second register of the same company is a second place their name can be wrong.
fields.label: Provider

fields.description: The crop this consultant advises on. EMPTY MEANS THE WHOLE OPERATION, which is the ordinary case for a farm with one consultant — it is not an unanswered question, and the reads say so rather than listing the row as incomplete. A firm covering pome fruit and not cherries is two rows, one per crop, because 'pome fruit' is a category this site's Crop register does not have and inventing one here would put a second vocabulary beside it.
fields.label: Commodity

fields.description: What they actually do: scouting, written recommendations, the whole IPM programme, application. Free text rather than a Select, because the arrangement a farm has with a consultant is not drawn from a list somebody wrote down once, and a Select would refuse the next one.
fields.label: Service Type

fields.description: The consultant's licence number where they hold one. Oregon licenses pesticide consultants under ORS 634, and a written recommendation from an unlicensed adviser is not a recommendation an inspector recognises. Left blank for an unlicensed adviser, which is a legitimate arrangement for scouting that stops short of a recommendation.
fields.label: Licence Number

name: Pest Management Provider
